title: Prakash v. M/s National Chemicals
text: The workman, Prakash, was retrenched by M/s National Chemicals citing factory closure due to losses. The workman raised an industrial dispute under the Industrial Disputes Act challenging the closure as colourable exercise of power. Evidence showed that the company did not follow the mandatory procedure under Chapter VB of the Industrial Disputes Act before closure, as the establishment employed more than 100 workmen. The Industrial Tribunal found the closure to be illegal and ordered reinstatement of all retrenched workmen with full back wages. The company challenged this. The High Court finds that Section 25-O of the Industrial Disputes Act mandates prior government permission for closure of large establishments. No such permission was obtained. The retrenchment is void. The reinstatement order is upheld. The workman is entitled to reinstatement with continuity of service and full back wages.
